chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man from the Ansar came to my father and said to him, 'I have been afflicted with a great matter. I have a slave girl whom I used to have intercourse with. One day I went to her, then I went out for a need of mine after having performed ghusl from her, and I forgot some maintenance money of mine. So I returned to the house to take it, and I found my slave girl on her belly. So I counted for her from that day of mine nine months, and she gave birth to a girl.'

He said, so my father said to him, 'It is not befitting for you to approach her, nor to sell her, but spend upon her from your wealth as long as you are alive. Then bequeath at your death that she should be spent upon from your wealth until Allah makes for her a way out.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a master who impregnates his slave girl regarding her status, sale, and maintenance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the specific legal status of a slave girl who becomes pregnant by her owner (Umm al-Walad), establishing that she is freed upon the owner's death. The Imam’s ruling emphasizes her continued financial support during the owner's lifetime and posthumously from his estate, highlighting the Shia scholarly emphasis on ensuring her dignity and freedom until she bears a child who will secure her emancipation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man from the Helpers came to my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I have been afflicted with a grievous matter. There is a slave girl for me, and I had gone to her. So one day I went to her, and then I went out regarding a need of mine, after having washed myself from her, and I forgot some expenses money from myself. So I returned to the house in order to take it, so I found my slave upon her belly. So I counted for her from that day of mine for nine months. So the slave girl gave birth’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘It is not befitting for you that you should go near her, nor sell her, but spend upon her from your wealth for as long as you are alive. Then bequeath during your death that they (inheritors) should spend upon her from your wealth until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Makes for her a way out’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from ibn Mahbub from ‘ Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

once a man from al-Ansar (people of al-Madinah) came to my father and said, ‘I am facing a huge problem. I have a slave-girl and I would go to bed with her. One day I went to bed with her, then went out for a certain work after taking Ghusl (bath); but I had forgotten something so I returned back home and found my slave on her belly. I counted nine months from that day and she gave birth to a girl.

My father said to him, ‘It is not proper for you to go close to her. Do not sell her. Spend for her from your assets as long as you live, and make a will to spend for her after your death from your assets until Allah makes a way out thereof.’”
